axes.model_access:
It calls no model itself. **The official docs state outright that this server is not intended to be a useful server** —
it exists for MCP client developers to test features against.

It implements prompts, tools, resources, sampling and other protocol features to showcase MCP capabilities.
axes.runtime:
A local Node.js process communicating over stdio.
A 2026-09-22 fix addressed subscription cleanup on session disconnect.
axes.local_files:
For testing purposes; it provides no real file-access capability.
The detailed resource and tool inventory is in the repo's `docs/features.md`.
axes.background: Not supported. It ends with the client process.
axes.tools:
19 tools in total; **this site has checked them one by one against the repo's `docs/features.md`** (2026-10-08):

- echo, get-annotated-message, get-env, get-resource-links,

- get-resource-reference, get-roots-list, gzip-file-as-resource,

- get-structured-content, get-sum, get-tiny-image,

- trigger-long-running-operation, toggle-simulated-logging,

- toggle-subscriber-updates, trigger-elicitation-request,

- trigger-url-elicitation, trigger-sampling-request,

- simulate-research-query, plus the two async variants of sampling / elicitation.

There are also 4 prompts and a batch of resource templates (also in features.md).
Output shapes are designed for demonstration targets, **not fit for direct consumption**.
axes.context: No cross-session memory. A test server — it offers no practical memory capability.
axes.permissions:
**Not for production use**; permission boundaries are not a design goal.
The official positioning is a testing tool — its permission hardening was never designed for production.
axes.fit:
**Fit for exactly one thing: testing whether your MCP client implements the protocol correctly.**
Not a fit for any real task scenario.

mcp.transport:
Supports stdio (default, launched via npx).
**The repo README documents two more remote forms** (verified 2026-10-08):
Streamable HTTP (`npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything streamableHttp`)
and SSE (the `sse` subcommand; officially marked deprecated since the 2025-03-26 spec).
mcp.scope:
**Not for production use.** As a testing tool, neither its permission scope nor its real operational capability
has been narrowed for production scenarios.
Before enabling it, make sure your environment is not exposed to risk as a result.

sectionTitles.与其他 reference server 的区别: How it differs from the other reference servers

sections.官方定位（原文）:
> This MCP server attempts to exercise all the features of the MCP protocol.
> **It is not intended to be a useful server**, but rather a test server for builders of MCP clients.
> It implements prompts, tools, resources, sampling, and more to showcase MCP capabilities.
sections.为什么仍然收录:
A comparison site that only lists "handy" tools would miss something important:
**what exists in the ecosystem for other purposes.**

Its inclusion value:

| Reader | What they get |
|---|---|
| MCP client developers | A test target with the broadest protocol coverage |
| MCP server developers | A reference implementation showing how protocol features are used |
| General readers | Learning to tell a "reference server" from a "usable server" |

**But it must never be recommended as a practical tool.**
sections.变更记录说明:
| Date | Content |
|---|---|
| 2026-09-22 | Clean up subscriptions on session disconnect |
| 2026-08-28 | Remove template URI validation and dead code in subscription cleanup |

**The 09-22 entry is a substantive fix**: subscriptions not cleaned up on session disconnect cause a resource leak.
sections.与其他 reference server 的区别:
| server | Positioning | Usable for real tasks |
|---|---|:---:|
| `filesystem` | Reference implementation | ✅ |
| `git` | Reference implementation | ✅ |
| `memory` | Reference implementation | ✅ |
| `sequential-thinking` | Reference implementation | ✅ |
| `fetch` | Reference implementation | △ needs a security assessment |
| `time` | Reference implementation | ✅ |
| **`everything`** | **Testing tool** | ❌ |

**This very comparison column is part of the site's value**: judging only by "they are all in the official servers repo"
makes them seem identical in nature. They are completely different.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs.

**What "measurement" means for this server is different**: what to test is not whether it can do work,
but whether your MCP client correctly handles every protocol feature it exposes.
The test checklist is in the repo's `docs/features.md`.
